about: Ransom's Rest (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.md), the first area of the Revenant campaign: a high valley in the Reaches, closed by ridges on the north, east and south, ending on the west at the Rim over Gravewind Canyon. Coordinates are Unreal world centimeters: X is north (+), Y east (+), Z up; (the doc's plan meters: X = y * 100, Y = x * 100). Heights relative to the valley's base (Z = 0). Built by Art/Models/Terrain/RansomsRest.py; checked by Tools/terrain_check.ps1 RansomsRest. The approved map's data is Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.plan.json.
name: RansomsRest

map.about: The core square (half its side, cm) and the cell size (cm) each raster aims at: 512 m at 12.5 cm heights since the mountain (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest_Expansion.md, section 6), grown from the 400 m square (grownFrom: the noise and the lip's outline worked out as that square had them, so the valley's heights came out the same: Tools/terrain_compare.ps1); caps lets the curvature and occlusion keep 20 cm, the scatter mask 25 cm and the macro map 6.25 cm, which macroSplit 2 paints as four 4096 px windows (RansomsRestMacroSW, SE, NW, NE), one per quarter of the square, each its own texture set worn by the tiles over it.

mesh.about: The top in 6 x 6 tiles over the map square (the macro map's windows' edges are tiles' edges), about 190k triangles; coarse lets Larkspur Bench's gentle meadow spread its vertices to 2.4 m where it barely bends, so the valley keeps its 1.2 m (Art/Levels/area_mesh.py); holes leaves the top open where an interior goes into the ground: the Providence's mouth in Larkspur High's band, framed by the portal model.

macro.about: The macro maps' ground: lateSummer paints the meadow as a mosaic of late summer's grass tones keyed to the ground (Art/Levels/area_mosaic.py), bleached straw on the rises through gold and olive to the green of the creek bottoms, in place of the island's meadow graded gold, which read as one flat ochre from the lookout (2026-10-08). shade: the living tree stands (obstacle ids) whose ground is darker and greener (every forest and orchard zone too); hayfields: the openGround polygons mowed into stubble, rows the mowing's heading (degrees, 0 north, 90 east); zones: moisture added by zone kind (a watered farm and orchard greener, the town, the depot and the wind-blasted point dustier). blooms colors the wildflower drifts by zone kind (hue: where on the mosaic's flower ramp, larkspur blue about 0.04; pull toward it; more: the drifts' density times this): the alpine meadow's blue larkspur.

places.about: Each place's own ground at eye level (2026-10-22, the user: the world looks samey; the tones above read only from the air): Art/Levels/area_places.py rasterizes these layers into T_RansomsRestPlaces_M (M_Terrain's PlaceMap: how much of each place's ground lies where) and T_RansomsRestPlacesScatter_M (the grass kept, the cinders', chips' and coal lumps' density), straight from this file (no terrain run). Each layer is one of the four GroundPlaces patterns (Tools/Blender/looter_textures.py: R the town's red-ochre street dust with wheel ruts along U (Main Street and the rail bed run along Y), hoof and boot prints; G ash with black cinders; B pale limestone grit and chips; A coal dust and lumps, which also serves the rail bed's black cinder ballast and the depot's coal dust), laid over its zones, features and roads (a road with [weight, reach m] carries the place's ground out along it, fading over reach: the path edges where roads meet a place), frayed at the edges and in patches; dark and light are the ends of its ramp (sRGB), own how much of them replaces the macro map's colour (the rest keeps the macro's light and dark), rough the roughness at the ramp's dark and light ends (coal lumps glint). Tools/Unreal/build_world_materials.py M_Terrain puts the map, PlaceRect (the core square), PlaceAmount and the colours on the instances named here. The scatter (Tools/Unreal/build_island_scatter.py) thins the grass and flowers to each layer's grass share and lays its clutter (pebble clusters and small chunks in instances: level.materials MI_PlaceCinder/Chalk/Coal_Ransom); the chapel knoll's white yarrow is its own listed layer there (yarrow).

scatter.about: The scatter mask (Art/Levels/area_scatter.py): roadside pebbles keeps every road's surface clear of stones and lines the roads with pebbles only, so no rock or boulder stands in Main Street, the yards, on the rail bed or across a junction; steep bare keeps every stone off ground too steep to walk up (the rock past the boundary, the cliffs' faces), where it would hang on the slope. layers: the meadow layers' own spacing (cm) and a factor on their shared cull distances (Tools/Unreal/build_island_scatter.py): the grass a little denser and reaching about 40 m on Medium instead of 27-33 m, the flowers 38 m, so the meadows don't turn to bare ground a few dozen meters out (2026-10-08; the macro map carries the grass's color past that). blooms: more flowers by zone kind (times): Larkspur Bench's larkspur drifts. The Bench's forest zones are lodgepole stands: pines only (Tools/Unreal/build_island_scatter.py's split should keep them to Pine_A and Pine_B).

region.about: The regional height field around the core (Art/Levels/area_region.py), in cm: the valley floor's noise and tilt (meters of rise per meter north and east) and its benches (a polygon raised or lowered by height, easing out over blend), the ridges (each from its foot: height, crest = how far behind the foot the crest is, back = the outer slope's reach, band = the cliff band at the foot; a saddle lowers the crest near a pass), the escarpment (its lip, the drop to the canyon floor, how deep the cliff kit's stacked courses reach, the far wall; calm keeps the lip from wandering where a model is fitted to it), the surround ring and the backdrop. The core's outer seamBand fades into the field; no feature may enter it. floors raises a hanging valley's ground to a level inside a polygon (the higher of the two, round: the smooth maximum's width; levels: four corners' heights over a rectangle, held past it; relief: rolling swells): Larkspur Bench behind Larkspur Ridge's crest, +44 m in the south-west to +58.5 m in the north-east; ridges marked onFloor stand on the floors (Larkspur High, the East Shoulder), and bandGaps leaves a ridge's band undressed where the Old Quarry cuts through it.

backdrop.about: The silhouettes past the ring (Art/Levels/area_beyond.py backdrop()): a curtain per layer, distance (cm) out, from base (or lower) up to a skyline over the bearing (0 north, 90 east). Each direction's [low, high] (cm) is the skyline's range, eased between them; relief adds low rolling swells, about that high (cm) either way per direction, wavelength (cm) apart along the circle; notches [bearing, width in degrees, depth (cm)] cut soft U gaps, a side canyon's. Mesas are the landforms standing on the range's low: [bearing, width, height] is the plain flat-topped mesa; [bearing, width, height, kind] or {azimuth, width, height, kind, side, tilt} picks mesa, butte, stepped, broken or spire (side -1 mirrors it, tilt lifts its far side). The landforms and gaps west are composed for Ransom's Point and the deck (bearing 247.5): two close together, a wide gap, the big stepped one, a spire, a broken one, the 6 km layer's peeking between; the nearest layer's relief and gaps east are for the ridge foot (bearing 85).

boundary.about: The playable boundary as approved (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.plan.json), corners [X, Y] in cm in order; open lists runs of open edges (from corner a to corner b), where a drop is part of play; blocked lists runs closed by something built (Stage Gap's mouth: the parked locomotive and the rockslide). The other edges stand at the foot of rock too steep to climb: the ridges' bands, and wherever a band stands back or fades, the rock foot makes (Art/Levels/area_boundary.py). Since the mountain the polygon takes in the Old Quarry, the Goat Steps' neck up to the crest and Larkspur Bench (its lip and its west end on the Rim open, Larkspur High's band and the East Shoulder rock); interiors splices the Providence's galleries in as a tongue under Larkspur High, after the surface corner at its mouth, for the game's polygon only (layout_computed.json): its edges closed, its corners at its floor, and the terrain's rules never see it.

foot.about: The rock past every other closed edge (Art/Levels/area_boundary.py): the ground stays level for setback (cm) past the line, then rises at slope (degrees) by at least height (cm) and on at back (degrees), easing into the ground behind by reach (cm). It never lowers the ground, so the ridges' bands stand as they are; it's the rule where a band stands back or fades. Tools/terrain_check.py holds the rise from the line to 5 m out over 44 degrees, its foot within 2.5 m, every 5 m along each edge.

openGround.about: The open-ground metric (Art/Levels/area_open.py): every walkable meter inside the boundary is measured to its nearest break (a building, wall, fence, outcrop or boulder group, tree stand, cliff, or a 1.5 m rise within 6 m). target is the most it should be (cm); open marks ground left open on purpose, which isn't measured (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.md: the hayfields, Main Street, the crossroads at the keeper's grave and the grave's line to the bell tower).

level.about: How Tools/Unreal/build_area.py builds the level (step 5a): the map, the tag and outliner folder of everything it places, the zones scattered trees keep out of ([zone id, share of its bounding box]), the scatter's PCG graph and volume (Tools/Unreal/build_island_scatter.py RansomsRest), and how far behind the closed edges the walls stand (wallSetback, cm: at the rock's foot, which rises about 2.5 m past the line). models: a placement kind's model where this area has its own (Grandma Delia's lived-in house, SM_Farmhouse_Ransom, for the farmhouse; the clapboard SM_Cottage_Ransom and the shake-roofed SM_Barn_Ransom for the tutorial island's cottage and barn). lights: the lived-in houses' lamps and lamplit windows, brighter at dusk (AHouseLights on each one's SOCKET_Light: the lamp's candelas by day and at dusk, its reach in cm), and the empty cottages' windows left dark. props: models only the build places, on the ground at their location (x, y cm), turned by yaw and tagged Obstacle like the placements; their footprints are the layout's obstacles already, so the generator needs nothing of them (the town gate over its posts, townGateNorth and townGateSouth). smoke: the buildings whose chimneys smoke (placement keys), in a half-empty town in mourning only the lived-in ones: Delia's, Pruitt's store, Tilly's, two cottages and the waiting locomotive. cliffs: the walls varied piece by piece (varied: the cliff groups), their tops reaching 72-112% of the wall (top) and one point in ten left out (gaps), so the ring at the valley's foot isn't one even picket wall; in the Sink (lean: its pit and ramp groups) every piece leans back with the generated wall behind it (measured by traces at build time), which slopes, so no piece stands buried in the slope with only its top poking out: from the floor those read as rocks hanging off the rim. materials and swaps: the area's own instances of shared materials, worn by everything the build places: the rock (MI_RockCliff_Ransom, on the cliff kit, the outcrops and Den Rock) warmer and darker than the tutorial island's pale cream, toward the valley's ochre, with only a little dry lichen on its tops in dry country (MossAmount 0.12 in a dusty grey-ochre MossColor, on the granite too: olive-green tops read damp), and the den's own rock (MI_RockCliffDen_Ransom: its pale tint times the same warming); the terrain's and the ring's steepest faces taking the rock from 40 degrees, full by 55 (MI_RansomsRestMacro_Steep, MI_RansomsRestRingMacro_Steep: the 35-50 degree faces dominate the views, and banded ochre past 50 read bare); the dressed granite blocks with no moss (MI_RockGranite_Ransom: bright moss turned the Sink's dead floor green); the orchard's leaves (MI_LeavesApple_Ransom) olive-amber with half the trees turning gold-amber (its apples are their own slot and stay red), late summer's, as the palette asks, and the scattered oaks and birches olive-drab and gold with a third of each turning (MI_LeavesOak_Ransom, MI_LeavesBirch_Ransom: Tint, and TintVariation on VariationAmount of the trees; the scatter takes the swaps as its override materials). The Sink keeps its own looks, set by build_area_sink.py on its pieces alone (not swaps): its floor's web mats in dusty silk (MI_Web_SinkFloor) and its dressed blocks in a dusty granite with no moss beside the walls (MI_RockGranite_Sink). In the Sink (lean: its pit and ramp groups) every piece leans back with the wall behind it, from the wall's real foot, and no top ends inside the wall's rounded lip (a top that would comes down under it; the ramp's walls spread their tops under it, leanTop, and stand 50 cm out from the wall, leanProud); runs that end at Den Rock reach into it (abut). The Sink's pit wall (panels: theSink) is dressed with the narrow cliff panels in short steps along its curve, each leaning with the wall and standing 0.55 m proud of its most forward point, tops under the lip, and the seam wedge in the corner by Den Rock (build_area_panels.py); its feet banked with talus (talus: Rocks.py's cliff-rock slabs and chunks a third buried every 1.5-2.5 m, with smaller chunks in front where the foot's gap is deep, laid by build_area_sink.py's gameplay pass clear of the sacs, the spiders' spots, the lantern, the blocks and the den's way out, with web mats between a few). The cliff pieces under the burial deck end under its boards (under): the escarpment's top course stood through the deck's open end. The windmill alone (swapsOn) trades its teal and orange rust for weathered galvanized steel (MI_MetalWorn_Windmill: the worn metal set tinted 0xb8b5ac), as the art brief keeps loot colours off the world; the barns, well and crates keep their rust.

environment.about: The golden hour tried out on Lvl_TerrainTest (Tools/Unreal/build_area_environment.py): the sun low in the west-southwest over the canyon, haze thickest down in the canyon and glowing warm toward the sun, the planet's top down on the plains, the cloud dome past the backdrop. Tuned on Ransom's Rest at step 5a. Art note 3 (the sky): the sky's own color cancels most of the warm sun's tint, so it stays a clear blue overhead and warms only toward the sun; the haze ends at 13.5 km, between the backdrop (12 km) and the cloud dome (15 km), so neither the sky nor the clouds wear it; the haze's glow toward the sun matches the warm sky there. Art note 2 (the far band): the fog thinned to 0.003 (dusk 0.004) and the atmosphere's own haze stretched 3 times, so the backdrop's layers fade by distance, darker near and paler far, instead of melting into one pale band; M_Backdrop darkens them toward the sun to their shaded sides.

Dusk.about: The scripted dusk (step 13; the cold open and Main 6, Looter.Light Dusk), tuned on Lvl_TerrainTest: the sun 4 degrees over the horizon a little further west, warmer and dimmer, its long shadows capped at 60 m; the sky light dimmer, recaptured behind the switch; the haze cooling to a dim violet away from the sun, still glowing amber toward it; the backdrop's ranges darkened and warmed through MPC_Lighting so none shows bright at sunset; the exposure lifted a little so the fight stays readable. Art note 3 (the sky): the ozone raised to 3.5 times Earth's and the sky's color corrected, so the sky away from the sun turns twilight's blue-violet while it still burns orange to pink around the sun; the sun at 3600 K rather than 3200 K, since the ozone reddens its light too; the clouds dimmed and warmed so their lit sides glow peach against the violet.

gameplay.about: No director: the story's encounters (Docs/Areas/RansomsRest.md, "Encounters stay on one level of ground") are placed with their missions by build_area_story.py and its build_area_<place>.py scripts, and what happens between them is encounters below (build_area_camps.py). The story's first arrival (spawnLanding) is a player start of its own beside the level's start by Ellis's grave; the depot's station carries Landing_Depot (build_area_travel.py).

levels.about: The creatures' levels (Docs/Progression.md, "Creature levels"; the user's call, 2026-10-12: never the player's, always where they stand), rising along the story: 1-2 near the start, 2-4 round the town and the fields, 4-6 for the Sink, the Webwood, the quarry and the west, the bosses above their ground. band: the lowest and highest own level here, before ranks (Restless and Gravebound +1, Soulfed +2, a boss +1); the station board shows it. zones: looked through in order, the first holding a spot gives the creatures there their levels, each rolled evenly from the first to the second; a zone is a layout zone, an obstacle, its own polygon, or a radius round a point (at). kinds: a boss or Legendary monster at a set level wherever it stands. A spawner group's or boss wave's own level, or a creature placed at a level other than its class's, is kept. Tools/Unreal/create_area_assets.py writes all of it into DA_Area_RansomsRest; Looter.Creatures.AreaLevels and Looter.Progression.Pacing read it here.

encounters.about: What happens between the story's fights (Docs/Polish/BorderlandsComparison.md, item 7): camps (a few creatures, a Restless leader and a Supply Crate), patrols (a pack walking a stretch of road there and back) and ambushes (they spring as the player walks onto a landmark's ground). Placed by Tools/Unreal/build_area_camps.py, checked by Looter.Encounters.Camps.Placement and .Gating (since 2026-10-21 the user's bigger fights: camps and patrols 5-8, ambushes and fights 6-10; set pieces, a setPiece block: build_area_setpieces.py, ASetPieceSpawner, once a session by their story flag), counted by Looter.Progression.Pacing (Docs/Progression.md). Layout cm, X north, Y east. after: the missions turned in before it's on; like every encounter it starts over when the level loads (the crates stay opened: the session keeps them). keepOut and storyFights are what they keep off: the safe zones and arrivals, and the scripted fights' grounds while those fights can happen (a fight during a main mission is over once a later main mission is turned in; a roaming group's ground is shared, only its spots kept clear). budget: main (on the story's path, counted before countedBefore's own fights), roaming (with the few roaming kills a normal play makes), optional (an explorer's).

Main Street turns safe only after Main 3 is turned in, and Tilly (Speaker_Tilly) keeps her window shut while it's on, so Main 3 can't be turned in over the fight: the zone comes on after it, never during. The Bell-Ringer stands on the Gilt Spur's balcony deck (found by tracing down off its facade), in the street under it if no deck is found. Softened 2026-10-23 (the user: "Soften early only"; it had killed a player standing still): four Basic ahead, then two and the Restless one behind (its rank sting with the second beat), the second push only once one of the first is left (or 40 s), so the pushes never stack; was 4 and a Restless, then 5, pushed at 3 left or 30 s.
